title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, artifact-grounded numeric outcomes, a methods clarification of provider-call accounting, and an evidence-based interpretation that attributes the near-zero marginal guarded benefit to validator ceiling effects in a curated task bank. Reproducibility is supported by the archived execution manifest and bundled artifacts.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Production adoption requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, command-ordering/workflow constraints, and higher-order safety invariants. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and prototype reports document this trend but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value delivered by sandboxed execution when the same generated candidate is inspected by both conditions. To address that gap we preregistered and ran a paired confirmatory study asking: under shared_initial_candidate semantics for synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) that same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with full run accounting; (3) a methods clarification of provider-call accounting under shared_initial_candidate semantics; and (4) an evidence-grounded interpretation and operational recommendations about when guarded stages add measurable detection value.
sections.related_work: Work combining LLM generation with deterministic validators, repair loops, and emulation is now common in NetOps and adjacent AIOps literature. Survey and architectural reports emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional—syntactic parsing, sequence/workflow constraints, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and runtime behaviors each require different V&V primitives [1]. Tool-focused case studies show that mature static verifiers have greatly expanded rule coverage but still miss some runtime-dependent behaviors, motivating layered emulation or sandboxing [2]. Empirical findings from program/specification verification and recent NetOps prototypes also indicate that generation+verification patterns can improve correctness, but the marginal utility of emulation depends heavily on validator coverage, emulator fidelity, and the input distribution [3]. Our paired design isolates downstream guarded-stage contributions by presenting the identical sampled candidate to both conditions (shared_initial_candidate), avoiding conflation with generation variability that many prior evaluations leave unresolved.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered as a paired binary confirmatory experiment (study id recorded in the archived bundle). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated over confirmatory samples. The preregistered plan targeted Npairs = 720 with a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 for power planning, fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, a deterministic missingness policy for parser failures, and pre-specified analysis procedures including a two-sided exact McNemar test and a bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples). Task generation, topology templates, and vendor abstractions. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from a structured task family that encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). The task bank abstracts three vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates; inclusion required vendor‑parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds. In this run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720. Model configuration and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) and the runtime record shows model_calls_used = 721 with stage accounting indicating one repair-stage call. The preregistration enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair exactly one sampled initial candidate was obtained and that identical candidate was consumed by both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded). This isolates downstream effects (emulation observations or repair) as the only source of between-condition discordance. Baseline validator specification. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic, rule-based checker that performs vendor-CLI syntactic parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against the required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraint checks (make-before-break, all_down_before_any_field_change), protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance testing. The validator emits a binary detection flag and a validator_trace describing parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after, and any violation codes. Guarded pipeline and sandboxed-emulation harness. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then executes the same normalized CLI commands in an automated sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology template and vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulator records runtime observations relevant to operational safety—interface admin transitions, concurrent-interface states, MTU/VLAN application effects, and basic reachability consequences—and maps selected runtime observations to guarded detections when they reveal violations not encoded in the static rule set. Repair policy and run accounting. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task, invoked only after the shared initial candidate and downstream observations were available for the guarded condition. The archived run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 with stage counts indicating 720 shared_initial generations and 1 repair-stage call. Provider-call audit fields and reconciliation (clarification). The execution audit records provider-call events rather than per-condition hypothetical calls. In that audit the key labeled "shared" enumerates provider calls that produced the single sampled initial candidate reused across both paired conditions (720 events), while the key labeled "guarded" enumerates provider calls associated with guarded-stage repair activity (1 event in this run). Thus the apparent asymmetry in those condition-count keys is an event-count asymmetry (initial-generation events vs. repair-stage events) and does not contradict complete_pair_count = 720. Complete accounting (completed_episode_count = 1440 and model_calls_used = 721) is internally consistent under the shared_initial_candidate contract because each pair consumed a single shared generation and only one additional repair call occurred across the entire confirmatory set. Analysis procedures. The primary confirmatory analysis followed the preregistered paired-binary executor: exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts, and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were pre-specified as exploratory with multiplicity adjustment.
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded numeric results). Complete paired counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). Discordant-pair attribution. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics any discordant guarded-only detection must arise from a guarded-stage emulation observation or from an allowed repair-stage invocation. The provider-call audit shows a single repair-stage model call across the confirmatory set; the single n10 discordant count is therefore attributable to that unique downstream event (repair-stage and/or guarded emulation observation). The archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts record the episode accounting and provider-call audit needed to locate and inspect that unique episode for auditors. Representative per-episode traces and validator_trace fields for non-discordant episodes uniformly report parsed_command_count and required_command_count consistent with the tasks’ required sequences and violation_count = 0 in the vast majority of cases, supporting the interpretation of a validator ceiling effect in this curated bank.
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded interpretation of the near-zero guarded benefit. The evidence supports three primary, artifact-grounded explanations for the negligible aggregate guarded-stage effect: (1) validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment: the deterministic validator explicitly encoded the syntactic and workflow checks exercised by the curated tasks, producing a baseline success rate of 719/720 and leaving little headroom for the emulator to add detections; (2) curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure: the confirmatory set required parser acceptance and came from a deterministic generator constrained to workflow patterns the validator was designed to catch, underrepresenting runtime-only faults common in noisier distributions; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity: because every pair reused the same sampled candidate and there was only one repair-stage call recorded, the single observed discordance maps to one downstream event rather than to broad guarded-stage coverage. Operational implications. For environments with a high-coverage static validator tailored to expected intent patterns and with strict parser-level prevalidation, adding a fully automated sandboxed-emulation stage may provide only marginal incremental detection benefit and may not justify the extra cost and latency at scale. By contrast, in operational regimes characterized by noisy natural-language intents, adversarial inputs, broader vendor/CLI diversity, or complex long-lived state transitions, guarded emulation is likely to surface runtime effects static rules miss. Practical recommendations. Operators may: (a) prioritize extending static validator coverage for common workflow patterns when throughput and low latency are primary goals; (b) deploy guarded sandboxing selectively for high-impact changes or high-risk classes of intents; (c) develop adversarial test banks to locate validator gaps and to determine where emulator investment yields a measurable marginal detection return. Evidence-grounded follow-up directions. The archived artifacts suggest three concrete, reproducible extensions: adversarially generated tasks aimed at validator gaps, broader vendor-CLI and syntactic diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation modeling vendor-specific control-plane subtleties. Those targeted extensions are the appropriate next step to identify regimes where guarded stages add substantive operational value.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; under shared_initial_candidate semantics the archived run accounting permits auditors to locate that episode and inspect downstream traces. We interpret the result as a near-zero marginal guarded benefit for this constrained experimental regime driven by validator ceiling effects and curated inclusion; whether that conclusion generalizes requires adversarial, multi-vendor, and higher-fidelity emulation follow-ups. The archived execution manifest and bundled artifacts provide the reproducible starting points for those extensions.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator‑ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) constrain broader generalizability across models and validator designs.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream guarded-stage contributions but remove potential benefits from independent re-generation in the guarded condition; this design choice narrows the interpretation of the paired difference.
Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the harness used; higher-fidelity emulation could change outcomes.

Power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime.
